title: EmberBank - Dedicated Capacity Discovery
header:
Date: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (EmberBank Head of ML), Ruth Patel (CTO), Marcus Lee (Infra), Ana Gomez (Security)
summary: Discovery focused on Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU sizing, isolation/VPC needs, burst strategy and autoscaling expectations. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, KV/prefix caching, quantization options, SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: send pricing & architecture doc, schedule 1-week pilot benchmark, share security pack and SSO details.

Schedule pilot kickoff (1-week benchmark) - target week of 2026-03-16
Share SOC2 + encryption docs and SSO integration guide
SE to prepare sample workload config and recommended GPU sizing
action_items: Sofia Martinez — Send pricing + architecture doc — due 2026-03-06
Daniel Cho — Prepare pilot plan and recommended instance sizes + burst policy — due 2026-03-10

transcript_text:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me OK?
[00:04] Ruth Patel: Yup, all good here.
[00:07] Liam O'Connor: Yeah thanks Sofia. We put together a little agenda — focused on Dedicated capacity questions.
[00:12] Sofia Martinez: Perfect, that's what we were planning for. I'll hand over to Daniel and Priya for the technical run, i'll cover commercial at the end.
[00:18] Daniel Cho: Great. quick context question — what's the primary workload? is it chat-heavy or bulk embedding?
[00:24] Liam O'Connor: Mostly chat + contextual summarization for customer support, some nightly batch embeddings for search reindex. Peak concurrency is roughly 800 concurrent chat sessions, average turn length ~40 tokens, but we have spikes during morning wave.
[00:37] Marcus Lee: And a note on infra — we want isolation, can't have multi-tenant compute on the same GPU host due to audits. VPC-only, private subnet, and keys rotated in customer KMS.
[00:46] Priya Rao: That aligns well with our Redwood Dedicated offering. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in your account, private networking and optional customer-hosted control plane for Private deployments. Quick Q: do you expect sustained throughput or is it bursty?
[00:58] Liam O'Connor: It's a mix — sustained baseline of about 200 concurrent chats, bursts up to 800 for 20-40 minute windows. We need predictable tail latency under 200ms for small prompts.
[01:09] Daniel Cho: Ok got it. For a baseline we typically size reserved capacity to cover your sustained baseline and add a burst pool for spikes. Our autoscaler can add ephemeral nodes from a burst pool, or you can use pre-warmed reserved nodes. There's also a policy to fallback to a slightly higher-latency but lower-cost model variant under extreme load.
[01:29] Ruth Patel: What's the difference in unit cost between burst ephemeral and reserved? we need to understand cost predictability.
[01:35] Sofia Martinez: The pricing sheet i'll send breaks that down — short answer: reserved is cheaper per GPU-hour and gives SLA, burst ephemeral is market-rate (higher) without SLA unless you pre-commit burst capacity. We'll include numbers.
[01:47] Marcus Lee: Security question — you said customer KMS, do we have HSM support and can we ensure no model weights or KV cache leave our VPC?
[01:56] Priya Rao: Yes, we support integration with customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption at rest. For Dedicated we can ensure models run in your VPC; KV cache lives in-memory on the serving nodes and we can configure retention policies. We also offer optional disk encryption if you persist cache shards.
[02:10] Ana Gomez: Are audit logs delivered to our S3? we need full request-level tracing for compliance.
[02:15] Daniel Cho: We can stream audit logs to your S3 or to Splunk/Datadog. Logs include request id, model variant, latency, and token counts. For PII redaction we can apply a masking step before logs are persisted.
[02:26] Liam O'Connor: On the model side, are you hosting both open models and proprietary ones? we might want to run a tuned internal model later.
[02:33] Priya Rao: We support open models in our catalog and you can bring-your-own-model (BYOM) for Private deployments. For Dedicated, we can host customer models if licensing permits; we also recommend quantization for cost savings.
[02:44] Ruth Patel: Quantization — how much savings and impact on latency/quality should we expect?
[02:49] Daniel Cho: Typically 4-bit quant gives 2-3x throughput improvement and lower memory, slight perf delta on hallucination-sensitive tasks; depends on model. We'll run evals against your prompt set in the pilot.
[02:59] Sofia Martinez: that's why the pilot is important — to validate quality and unit economics.
[03:03] Marcus Lee: For autoscale, how fast can burst instances come up? those 20-40 minute surges are tough.
[03:09] Priya Rao: If you use our warm pool strategy, you can maintain a small fleet of pre-warmed GPUs that can take traffic in seconds. Cold-start ephemeral from cloud can be a few minutes depending on provisioning and image pulls. We typically recommend a hybrid: reserved baseline + warm pool sized for 50-60% of expected spike, with autoscale filling remaining headroom.
[03:28] Liam O'Connor: And if we can't accept slightly higher latency during extreme spikes, can you route overflow to hosted Redwood API instead of dropping requests?
[03:36] Daniel Cho: Yes, smart routing can failover to hosted with policy controls. Note that data residency and compliance must be considered — routing to hosted means requests leave your VPC unless you have a Private deployment with routing policies.
[03:49] Ruth Patel: What's the SLA for Dedicated?
[03:52] Sofia Martinez: For Dedicated we offer a 99.9% uptime SLA on the control plane and guaranteed reserved capacity, with latency SLOs in the contract depending on instance type. We'll include the SLA terms in the contract.
[04:02] Ana Gomez: Do you have SOC 2 Type II and encryption certs?
[04:06] Sofia Martinez: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have organizational controls documented; i'll attach the security pack. We also have ISO 27001 in progress, and customer-specific contractual addenda for enterprise.
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: For the pilot, what telemetry do you need from our side?
[04:22] Daniel Cho: We'll ask for a representative prompt set, sample conversation traces, and expected concurrency patterns (per-region). Also input/output sizes and any PII requirements for handling. We'll share an eval harness we run inside the Dedicated environment.
[04:34] Ruth Patel: Is there an option to run this on-prem with airgap later?
[04:38] Priya Rao: Yes — Redwood Private supports on-prem packages. It requires longer lead time for packaging and compliance but it's a path. For most customers, Dedicated VPC hits the compliance bar faster.
[04:48] Marcus Lee: Implementation timeline? If we say yes to pilot next week, how long to spin up baseline dedicated nodes in our AWS account?
[04:54] Daniel Cho: For baseline reserved nodes in an existing cloud account, we can provision in 3-5 business days assuming networking is ready. Burst warm pool might add a couple days. Private on-prem is multi-week.
[05:05] Sofia Martinez: Commercially we can offer a short-term credit for the pilot to cover cloud-hours while we validate.
[05:10] Liam O'Connor: Great. Any constraints on model licensing if we bring our own LLM?
[05:14] Priya Rao: Licensing depends on the model vendor; we require confirmation that you have rights to host it. For some models we can also handle hosting under our agreement if needed.
[05:22] Ruth Patel: Back to cost — could you show an example with GPU types? like A100 vs H100 cost and perf?
[05:28] Daniel Cho: Sure — in the pricing sheet we'll show per-token cost estimates for A100 and H100, plus 4-bit quantized variants and recommended batch sizes. H100 typically gives lower latency on long-context but is more expensive per-hour.
[05:40] Ana Gomez: Data residency — we need all traffic to remain in EU region for GDPR. Can Dedicated be region-locked?
[05:46] Priya Rao: Yes, you can pin Dedicated pools to a region and enforce routing policies. We also support region-specific model catalogs.
[05:54] Liam O'Connor: Who will be our day-to-day contact during pilot?
[05:58] Sofia Martinez: i'll be primary for commercial and coordination, Daniel will be SE for technical. Priya will support rollout headaches.
[06:05] Ruth Patel: Ok let's recap next steps.
[06:07] Sofia Martinez: Recap — Redwood sends pricing and dedicated architecture doc by Friday, SE prepares pilot plan and instance size recommendations, EmberBank shares compliance checklist and representative prompts. We'll schedule pilot kickoff for week of March 16. Anything to add?
[06:22] Marcus Lee: Please include sample network diagram and S3 logging details.
[06:26] Ana Gomez: And encryption/hsm integration steps.
[06:29] Liam O'Connor: Also include a quick cost scenario for 200 baseline vs 800 peak.
[06:34] Sofia Martinez: will do. Thanks all, we'll follow up in email and set the calendar for pilot kickoff.
[06:40] Ruth Patel: Thanks, bye.
[06:42] Daniel Cho: bye everyone.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps, speaker overlap around 03:03-03:09 where multiple people spoke. References to KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K V cache" or "kayvee cache" in earlier systems.
